title: End-to-End Model Compression for Personalized Neural Speech Codecs
abstract: Neural speech coding (NSC) leverages deep learning to achieve high-quality speech compression, surpassing conventional methods. However, recent NSC models have grown substantially in size and complexity, limiting their feasibility for real-time processing on resource-constrained devices. To address this issue, we propose a speaker-aware model compression framework for end-to-end NSC. In this approach, speakers are clustered by perceptual similarity, and both encoder and decoder are trained with group-specific data, reducing computation while preserving perceptual quality. Subjective listening tests show that the proposed method reduces the model size by 96% and the bitrate by 50% (from 2 kbps to 1 kbps), while maintaining the perceptual quality of the state-of-the-art Descript audio codec (DAC). Moreover, the personalized models remain robust under noisy conditions, consistently outperforming baselines under acoustic distortions. These results highlight the feasibility of deploying NSC on low-power devices in both clean and noisy environments.
relevance_note: Speaker-aware end-to-end compression of neural speech codecs; codec design for speech.
